concerns.message: Finding 6 misreads §12, and decisions.md repeats the misreading. The §12 row 'Both duel clients absent' says to 'Cancel unresolved rewards if both forfeit on the same tick'. Separately, 'Disconnect in duel' says to forfeit after 10 seconds absent, and §12 adds that 'if they remain absent, the ordinary forfeit rule applies'. So if A's window expires while B is still inside B's own window, A forfeits and B wins. That is what the snapshot does. The only real gap is the same-tick case: two expiries that land on one frame, where the first onLeave invents a winner by processing order. §7 forbids exactly that ('processing order cannot invent a winner'). The task's rule, 'when the opponent is also disconnected, end the duel with no winner', is broader than §12. It takes a win away from a player who drops briefly and would return in time. It also lets a losing player escape the loss if the opponent drops at the right moment. decisions.md's own Deferred item describes the ledger gap as 'both forfeit on the same tick', which shows the intended rule is the narrow one.
concerns.consequence: The worker writes an integration test that locks in a rule contradicting §12. The general reviewer, reading §12, can flag it. encounters-theft would then inherit a room forfeit rule that differs from the spec's reward rule and have to rework it. The operator should choose now between two options. (a) Spec-literal: an ordinary forfeit on the first expiry, and a cancel only when both expiries fall on the same duel frame, with forfeits deferred to the frame boundary and evaluated together. (b) The broader cancel, recorded as a deliberate deviation from §12.

concerns.message: Finding 2 asks for 'the minimum with no impairment' as an exact assertion on a live measurement. Input delay is chosen from round-trip and jitter measured over real sockets during a 3 s countdown. This machine is shared, and other runs' vitest and Playwright compete for its event loop. At 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 %, a lost probe causes a head-of-line stall of about 200 ms and can push the measurement to the 8-frame cap. Whether a probe is hit depends on how the seeded loss lines up with the message sequence.
concerns.consequence: The integration check becomes flaky: 4 frames where 3 was expected under load, or out of the band when a probe is stalled. A candidate that is otherwise correct fails verification. Put the exact mapping in a unit test of the pure selection function with fixed RTT and jitter samples. In the harness, assert impaired delay > unimpaired delay, both within 3..8, and the unimpaired delay ≤ minimum+1, or document why the band holds when a probe is stalled.

concerns.message: The integration test must import `apps/web/src/devLatency.ts` from `tests/integration`. Root `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json` over `tests/**/*.ts` with `moduleResolution: nodenext` and `types: ["node"]`, without `vite/client`. It therefore type-checks devLatency.ts and everything it imports under Node rules, unlike the web app's bundler config. If devLatency.ts reads `import.meta.env`, uses extensionless relative imports, or pulls in Phaser or the web client modules, typecheck fails even though vitest runs the test fine. The only precedent, `tests/e2e/sea.spec.ts` importing `palette.js`, is a leaf module.
concerns.consequence: The typecheck check fails after the tests pass locally. Keep devLatency.ts a leaf module: `.js` import specifiers, no `import.meta.env`, which the caller should read, and no DOM globals such as `location` or `window`.

concerns.message: `git checkout <ref> -- .` only writes the files in the snapshot tree. It never deletes files that duel-online-001 removed or renamed relative to b8c2934. The statement that the restore 'changes only paths this lane owns' checks what the snapshot added, not what it deleted.
concerns.consequence: Stale files left from a rename could break typecheck or build, or duplicate a test, and nobody would know why. Diff with `--diff-filter=DR` between b8c2934 and cb8fe85 before restoring, or restore with `git read-tree`/`git restore --source=cb8fe85 --worktree --staged .` limited to the owned paths.

concerns.message: Finding 1's integration test assumes the room measures round-trip with application messages that pass through the wrapped transport. If the RTT probe uses Colyseus's built-in ping, or a message handler registered before the wrap, the dev latency never reaches the measurement. The chosen delay can then stay at 3 unless the configured RTT is large enough to cross the first frame threshold (roughly ≥120 ms, depending on the policy).
concerns.consequence: The test either can't show the input delay rising, or it passes only because the worker chose an extreme latency. It would not show that the setting covers the probes the operator's playtest depends on. Wrap the headless client at the same seam the browser uses, and choose an RTT whose expected frame count is computed from the policy.

concerns.message: Finding 7 ('keep stepping to the last bundle's frame' after the phase becomes over) needs a hard stop at the final confirmed frame. Without one, the accumulator keeps predicting past the KO or timeout, and stepDuel runs on a finished duel.
concerns.consequence: After the result, the HUD's clock or health could drift past the authoritative values. That breaks duel-online's 'both views show the same health, clock and result' check intermittently. Clamp to the final bundle's frame and assert equality with the server's final snapshot.

concerns.message: The integration suite already takes about 102 s against a 300 s timeout, on a shared machine. The new tests each need a live room: dev-latency with and without delay (two countdowns plus probe windows), the double-absence test (10 s reconnection windows) and the stalled-bundle cases, if they go live. Per-test timeout is 20 s, so the absence test needs its own longer timeout.
concerns.consequence: Under load the suite drifts toward the 300 s cap, or the absence test hits the 20 s per-test timeout. Keep the resync and de-duplication cases (findings 4 and 5) as pure netcode unit tests. Share one room setup for the no-latency and delayed runs where possible.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Keep the plan's scope but move the timing-sensitive assertions below the network. First, unit-test the pure input-delay selection function (RTT and jitter samples → frames) for the exact values. In the harness and the dev-latency integration test, assert only relative, banded facts: delayed > undelayed, within 3..8. Keep findings 4 and 5 entirely in pure netcode and view unit tests. Second, for finding 6, implement §12 literally: an ordinary forfeit on the first expiry, and no winner only when both expiries resolve on the same duel frame, evaluated together at the frame boundary. That is a smaller change than the broader cancel rule and matches the spec's own wording.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Before any code changes, restore the snapshot in a scratch worktree and run only the harness integration test 5 times at each setting (no impairment, and 80/20/1) while the machine is under its usual shared load. Record the printed inputDelay and measured RTT and jitter. At the same time, read DuelRoom's onLeave and forfeit path and the RTT probe path. If the unimpaired delay is always the minimum and the impaired delay always falls in one narrow band, the exact assertions from finding 2 are safe. Otherwise switch to relative assertions. The same reading also shows whether the probes go through the transport seam that devLatency wraps, and so whether finding 1's integration test can work as specified.
